answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with a slow trust spiral: every new identity starts with a tiny transaction cap, and only earns a larger cap after a long history of verified, useful work. A forger can forge hundreds of fresh identities, but each one stays at the bottom rung, so cloning multiplies paperwork, not power. All completed work is published to a shared reef of auditable records, where peers check provenance; identities with copied or identical histories are merged and discounted. Attacking at scale then costs more real work than it can ever extract.
